whole_file.note: Complete-cost LOSS reproduced on this corpus: no VOLE lane, indexed or not, approaches gzip/zstd/xz/brotli. The indexed lane is 146,711 B larger than the non-indexed lane (the observation index record); it buys query capability, not size. The auto winner stays the non-indexed lane because auto is size-based.

query_court.correctness_method: each served slice cmp'd against the source slice; the whole descriptor verify'd (length + SHA-256) once
query_court.pre_registered: frozen before measuring: 6 byte-ranges (256 B at 0/1/8/16/24/31 MiB) + 8 --pdf-stream + 4 --pdf-object spans

h1_evaluation.hypothesis: For queries with output <= 1 MiB at >= 50% into a >= 32 MiB document, the indexed lane processes <= 25% of the bytes gzip -9 inflates and is >= 2x faster, byte-exact.
h1_evaluation.bytes_criterion_met: 8/8 (VOLE processes 1.4%-2.3% of the bytes gzip inflates)
h1_evaluation.cpu_time_criterion_vs_zstd_met: 0/8 (zstd decompresses the same prefix in ~0.00-0.01 s, faster than VOLE everywhere)
h1_evaluation.result: H1 MET vs gzip and xz in the late region; NOT met vs zstd; NOT met in the early region (<= ~8 MiB).

verdict: PARTIAL / SCOPED POSITIVE. Random-access decode work and decode CPU are genuinely reduced for mid/late queries (>= ~20x fewer bytes processed, ~2-5x faster than gzip/xz), byte-exact on all 18 queries. But v1 reads the whole descriptor, so on-disk I/O is NOT reduced (VOLE reads its full 17.5 MB .voldoc vs gzip's ~9.8 MB compressed prefix at 31 MiB); peak RSS is ~38 MB (a whole-descriptor parse) versus gzip's ~1.2 MB; zstd's raw decoder is faster on wall time at every point; and whole-file size still loses ~3x to xz. A seek/mmap reader is required before any I/O win can be claimed.
